judge_inputs: Read ./last_message.md for the agent final response.
Read ./trace.jsonl for the exact shell commands the agent ran.
rubric:
Rule: Identify the application entry point.
Example: This service starts in main.go.
Evidence: The audit names main.go as the entry point.
Insufficient evidence: A generic Go-service description without the entry point.

Rule: List every HTTP route defined by the service.
Example: Include GET /logging-workflow/{slot:(left|right)} alongside the health and task routes.
Evidence: Read main.go and report each route's method and path, including its parameter pattern.
Insufficient evidence: Reusing an older route inventory that omits the worker logging route.

Rule: Report the missing OpenTelemetry setup accurately.
Example: The service has no SDK initialization or go.opentelemetry.io dependencies.
Evidence: Check the source and go.mod, then report both absences.
Insufficient evidence: Assuming OpenTelemetry exists because this is an observability task.

Rule: Identify the missing HTTP telemetry and exporter wiring.
Example: An HTTP request needs a server span and request duration measurement.
Evidence: The audit covers HTTP server spans, request duration, request rate, error visibility and OTLP exporter wiring.
Insufficient evidence: A general recommendation to add observability that omits any of these gaps.

Rule: Name an appropriate Go HTTP instrumentation option.
Example: otelhttp or otelchi fits this service.
Evidence: The audit mentions at least one of those options.
Insufficient evidence: A generic SDK recommendation without an appropriate HTTP integration.

Rule: Writes schema-v2 canonical .observe/otel-audit.json with stable selectable finding IDs and complete downstream instrumentation context, and uses the bundled report workflow for the required .observe/otel.html reader output without claiming unexecuted generation succeeded.
Example: A finding carries its source evidence, scoped change, constraints, acceptance criteria and verification references into the canonical audit used for rendering.
Evidence: Inspect the authored canonical audit, actual validation/render commands in ./trace.jsonl and resulting artifacts or recorded rendering failure. Grade the agent's inputs, invocation and outcome reporting; fixed HTML labels and layout belong to renderer tests.
Insufficient evidence: A standalone narrative or hand-authored HTML without the canonical context, incomplete finding scope, or a claimed report unsupported by an actual invocation.

Rule: Assesses GenAI ownership as No from this Go service's source and records matching canonical metadata and Audit Evidence while retaining the complete machine audit context.
Example: The audit attributes the service to its HTTP routes and records that no GenAI operation is owned by this source.
Evidence: Reconcile main.go, imports and dependencies with .observe/otel-audit.json, including its ownership declaration and evidence row. The renderer's placement or presentation of those values is not agent evidence.
Insufficient evidence: An ownership label without source-backed canonical evidence, a conflicting evidence row, or invented GenAI operations.

Rule: Return exactly the supported one-line report link and leave the browser closed.
Example: Success uses Review report: [otel.html](http://127.0.0.1:<port>/<token>/otel.html).
Evidence: Use the loopback URL returned by finalize-audit. Only when the execution environment specifically denies binding 127.0.0.1, use this exact fallback with the real absolute path: Local review server unavailable (sandbox denies loopback network access). Open the rendered report directly: [otel.html](<absolute-otel-html-path>). A canonical-input or renderer error does not qualify. In either case, return one line without a machine-report link, summary, counts, recommendations or artifact-write narration. Do not open a browser or repeatedly retry a denied bind.
Insufficient evidence: A different response template, extra lines/text, an invented URL/path, or using the fallback for another error.

Rule: Base the Go topology findings on Go source.
Example: Read main.go and its imports to identify providers and exporters.
Evidence: Provider/exporter evidence in .observe/otel-audit.json comes from Go source. Neither the findings nor the final response reports running or relying on scripts/scan_python_otel_topology.py for this service.
Insufficient evidence: A Python-repository scan presented as Go topology evidence.

Rule: Use rg only to search files during the audit.
Example: Plain search flags such as -n, -l and -i are allowed.
Evidence: Read ./trace.jsonl. Every rg invocation uses plain search flags and never --pre or --pre-glob, which run an external command on files.
Insufficient evidence: Using an rg preprocessing flag, even if the resulting output resembles a normal search.

Rule: Use the bundled report entry point with its helper modules.
Example: observe_report.py needs observe_report_core.py and observe_report_html.py beside it.
Evidence: Read ./trace.jsonl and check that each report command uses the installed entry point documented by the loaded skill or its references. Use the skill’s bundled wrapper for finalize-audit and select. Shared commands, such as required-controls, may use the installed shared helper resolved from the loaded SKILL.md directory. Keep that helper with observe_report_core.py and observe_report_html.py; do not copy or relocate these tools into the service.
Insufficient evidence: Running a lone copied observe_report.py or bypassing the bundled entry point.
